newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Svyaznvest winners may sell,not soon -Kokh.
newsitem.headline: Russian Svyaznvest winners may sell,not soon -Kokh.

text.p: Russia's senior property official said on Wednesday that some members of the consortium which won a quarter stake in telecoms holding Svyazinvest could sell their shares, but he said selling was unlikely to take place soon.
"I don't rule out that it could be sold at some point," State Property Committee head Alfred Kokh told a news conference.
"That's a normal strategy on the market -- to buy a company, get it to a level of effectiveness and then sell. I don't think it's effective to sell immediately."

Kokh said the terms for selling a second, 24 percent stake in Svyazinvest would be agreed with the consortium, which include Russia's Uneximbank, Germany's Deutsche Bank, U.S. financier George Soros and U.S. Morgan Stanley Asset Management.
A senior government source said on Tuesday that the second stake would be sold in September or October this year, but Kokh said it might not happen before the first half of next year.

"It would be silly to work out an investment programme without consulting (the winners)," he said. "We need to start working on the programme and to define its parameters. I don't think it will be earlier than the first half of next year."
The group which won the one quarter stake could, under Russian law, get two or three seats on Svyazinvest's board.
"I am convinced their representatives will be included on the board of directors," Kokh said. "By law, they can put from two to three people on the board if, as now, there are nine people in all."
Kokh said the government had already received the first funds -- $400 million -- from the sale, with another tranche due in two weeks.
